$comment: Mission 1.66.2 Part E. Post-30-day retention, re-read verbatim.
mission: 1.66.2 — ONYPHE Public Documentation Reconciliation & Configuration-Metadata Closure V1

retention_horizons.$comment: Part E1. Quoted from the Historical Data Availability page.
retention_horizons.note_on_the_two_categories_this_arc_comp: datascan keeps seven months and ctiscan one. The category carrying the protocol-native evidence is the one with the longer horizon, and the one whose port membership is published is the one with the shorter.

the_optimisation_sentence.$comment: Part E1 and E2. The load-bearing sentence, quoted exactly, typo included.
the_optimisation_sentence.verbatim: We keep the last 30 days of data will all the fields and up-to 16KB of raw application responses. For data older than 30 days, we remove some fields as they are less useful, and we truncate data field to 4KB.

two_operations_not_one.REMOVED: some fields, and the sentence does not name any of them
two_operations_not_one.why_the_distinction_holds: The sentence names the field it truncates and does not name the fields it removes. Mission 1.63 read it the same way and the reading is confirmed verbatim here.

raw_response_field.$comment: Part E2. B3 is not reopened.
raw_response_field.documented_as: raw application response received from the scanned service. Stored as full-text searchable content up to 1 MB.
raw_response_field.effect_on_the_construct: The predicate is a literal prefix of tens of bytes at the start of an identification string. A four-kilobyte truncation does not reach it.
raw_response_field.the_temptation_refused: Reading truncation as removal would reopen B3 and would be wrong. Reading truncation as harmless in general would also be wrong; it is harmless for THIS predicate because the predicate lives at the beginning of the field.

location_fields.$comment: Part E3. Each field independent. Silence is UNKNOWN.
location_fields.$note: The data model documents that these fields EXIST and what they mean. No page states whether they survive the 30-day boundary.

ip.documented_definition: the IP address of the scanned Internet asset. Supports CIDR range searches up to /8.
ip.basis: no first-party page names it among the removed fields, and none names it among the retained ones

@timestamp.documented_definition: timestamp of when the data was collected. Allows tracking when a given service or vulnerability was last observed.

node.id.documented_definition: unique identifier of the scanner node that performed the scan.

node.country.documented_definition: logical country the scanner node is assigned to (may differ from physical location).

node.physicalcountry.documented_definition: physical country where the scanner node is located.

arguments_available_and_refused.$comment: Part E3. Each of these would resolve a field favourably from something other than documentation.
arguments_available_and_refused.the_archive_would_be_useless_without_add: An argument from what a sensible provider would do. It is not what this provider documents.
arguments_available_and_refused.historical_querying_proves_timestamps_su: Historical querying proves that records are reachable in a past range. It does not prove which fields those records still carry, and the same sentence that grants seven months also says some fields are removed.
arguments_available_and_refused.the_fields_are_documented_so_they_are_re: The data model describes the schema. A schema says what a field means, never how long it lives.
arguments_available_and_refused.the_rule: Silence is UNKNOWN. An unnamed removed field is not guessed in either direction, including when the favourable guess is the one a sensible provider would make true.

verdict.what_did_change: Nothing about the verdicts. What is new is that the retention page was re-read verbatim for this exact question and still names only the truncated field, so the three UNKNOWNs rest on a directed reading rather than on an incidental one.
verdict.why_it_is_load_bearing: A count over a past window needs each observation to be attributable to an address, a time and a vantage. If any of the three is dropped beyond thirty days, an older observation stops being locatable, and the window the construct names is longer than thirty days.
